summary: @addai/node daemon polls hardcoded Supabase project and executes remote-supplied requests as PTY AI-agent sessions with permissions bypassed on the installer host
details: The `ainode` daemon in dist/session-runner.js polls a hardcoded Supabase project (syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co) via the RPCs `runtime_pick_next_request` and `runtime_commands_pick` and drives each remote-supplied row into a node-pty spawn of Claude/Codex/Kimi/Gemini/Grok. Prompts, working directory, model, allowed-tools, and environment for each spawn are taken from the remote row; the Claude launcher is invoked with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and pre-accepted settings so the agent TUI does not prompt. dist/command-runner.js additionally drains commands from the same backend and dispatches `install_harness` (running `npm install -g <spec.npmPackage>`), `login` (writing remote-supplied codes/API keys into third-party CLIs via PTY), `logout` (deleting credential files), `update_runtime` (`npm install -g` + respawn), and `set_autostart` (installing launchd, Windows Run, or systemd autostart entries). Whoever controls the paired backend account can thereby execute arbitrary shell/filesystem/network operations on the installer's machine through the AI agents, install additional npm packages globally, seed credentials, and establish persistence. dist/capabilities.js line 185 also modifies PATH and touches ~/.kimi/config as part of the harness setup.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
